original.prompt: In August 2026, the US Senate passed a bill authorising tariffs on buyers of Russian oil. Consider the following statements about the bill:
items: As first proposed, the bill sought a blanket 500 per cent tariff on any country doing business with Russia's energy sector.
The version passed by the Senate fixes a uniform 100 per cent tariff on all the named countries.
The applied tariff on the named countries is to be reassessed every 180 days.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The Senate version does not fix a uniform rate: the US Trade Representative can set the tariff anywhere from zero to 100 per cent on the named countries. The bill passed the Senate 86-11 and still needs to pass the House in identical form before it goes to Trump for assent.
original.source: The US Trade Representative can set the applied tariff anywhere from zero to 100 per cent on the named countries, which will be reassessed every 180 days.

rewritten.prompt: In August 2026, the US Senate passed a bill authorising tariffs on buyers of Russian oil. Consider the following statements about the bill:
items: As first proposed, the bill sought a blanket 500 per cent tariff on any country doing business with Russia's energy sector.
The version passed by the Senate narrows its scope to the five largest importers of Russian oil and gas.
The applied tariff on the named countries is to be reassessed every 180 days.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: All three statements are correct. The bill began as a blanket 500 per cent tariff, but the Senate version narrows it to the five largest oil and gas importers, with the US Trade Representative setting a rate from zero to 100 per cent that is reassessed every 180 days. The bill passed the Senate 86-11 and still needs to pass the House in identical form before it goes to Trump for assent.
rewritten.source: What passed the Senate narrows that to the five largest oil and gas importers, with a separate carve-out shielding countries that account for less than 15 per cent of Russia's total gas exports and are actively cutting that share.
